pr_title: [Python] Add support for strided `float32` and `float64` data
pr_body:
This PR fixes #5253 

The functionality was already mostly there, as other POD column dtypes already supported strided memory layouts, but somehow floating points got left behind.

issue_context.title: Creating table from pandas dataframe produces incorrect results
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

I create a table from a pandas DataFrame. When I select the data back out, the data is different from the input.

### To Reproduce

I've attached the `example.pkl` file inside a zip. 

[example.pkl.zip](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/files/9962969/example.pkl.zip)

```
import duckdb
import pyarrow as pa
import pandas as pd
import pickle

con = duckdb.connect()
with open('example.pkl', 'rb') as f:
    in_df = pickle.load(f)
# Replacing the load from pandas with a load from pyarrow produces correct results.
# in_tbl = pa.Table.from_pandas(in_df)
# con.execute('create table tiles as select * from in_tbl')
con.execute('create table tiles as select * from in_df')
out = con.execute('select * from tiles limit 10000').fetch_df()
print(in_df['alpha0'])
print(out['alpha0'])
```

Output:
```
0    0.011102
1    0.011101
2    0.011111
3    0.011123
4    0.011102
5    0.011101
6    0.011111
7    0.011123
8    0.011139
9    0.011137
Name: alpha0, dtype: float32
0    0.011102
1    0.102584
2    0.114941
3    0.104812
4    0.099318
5    0.104231
6    0.099771
7    0.106665
8    0.103630
9    0.100998
Name: alpha0, dtype: float32
```

Also note that saving the dataframe to CSV and then reloading it also fixes the issue. So, I'm guessing this is an edge case where the pandas data is stored 

Thank you!!

comments:
The issue originates in `vector_conversion.cpp:454`
```c++
			} else {
				// Otherwise we have to get it through 'to_numpy()'
				bind_data.numpy_col = py::array(column.attr("to_numpy")());
			}
```
this is equivalent to `df['alpha0'].array.to_numpy()` but somehow this results (when taking the data with `pybind11::array::data()`) in:
(result of that is stored in `numpy_col_data`)
```
(lldb) p ((float*)numpy_col_data)[0]
(float) $1 = 0.0111023095
(lldb) p ((float*)numpy_col_data)[1]
(float) $2 = 0.102584355
(lldb) p ((float*)numpy_col_data)[2]
(float) $3 = 0.114940837
```

Oh.. the shape is skewed, this is a row-major order array, we expect a column-major array
Maybe we need to add a detection for the order of a numpy array, and either convert it to column-major order or create a separate conversion path for row-major ordered dataframes

Ah, according to a random stack overflow comment, pandas can do this whenever it wants to
> The problem is that pandas DataFrame has an internal BlockManager which will consolidate columns with same dtype into a single contiguous memory block.

So it's not at all uncommon for this to happen..

We likely want to do something along the lines of:
https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/python/pybind11/+/9946bf3a509dc8c10255c1a64718624ecc537b0d/include/pybind11/numpy.h line 885
```


// Reference to element at a given index
--
  | template<typename... Ix> const T& at(Ix... index) const {
  | if ((ssize_t) sizeof...(index) != ndim())
  | fail_dim_check(sizeof...(index), "index dimension mismatch");
  | return *(static_cast<const T*>(array::data()) + byte_offset(ssize_t(index)...) / itemsize());
  | }


```
accessible through https://pybind11.readthedocs.io/en/stable/advanced/pycpp/numpy.html#direct-access

Got it working, basically just needed to port the code we already had for regular columns, floating point got left behind for some reason

Now the tricky part; creating a test that creates the problematic data layout 🙃
You're welcome, it was very low hanging fruit tbh :)

review_comments: Might not be worth it to separate these two cases, as we need to loop over the data regardless to check for NaN
